questions.question: Q: Explain two different Christian beliefs about creation.
questions.correctAnswer: 1) Literalist Christians believe Genesis describes actual events — God literally created the world in six 24-hour days, making all life forms directly. 2) Non-literalist Christians read Genesis as conveying theological truth (God is creator) but not scientific fact; they accept the Big Bang and evolution as the means God used to create, viewing the "days" as symbolic periods of time.

questions.question: Q: How does John 1:1-3 contribute to Christian understanding of creation?
questions.correctAnswer: John 1:1-3 presents Jesus (the Word/Logos) as the agent of creation, existing with God from the beginning. This expands the Genesis account by connecting creation to the Trinity — God the Son was active in creation, not just God the Father. It shows that creation was a Trinitarian act and that Jesus was not just a human teacher but divine from the beginning.
